newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity settles higher in choppy session.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity settles higher in choppy session.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Thursday, erasing early losses in another choppy session amid firm natural gas prices and stronger physical power values.
The electricity complex repeated similar trading patterns of the past several days, moving in lock-step with natural gas prices, brokers and traders said.

NYMEX January 1997 Henry Hub natgas futures settled up 3.6 cents at $3.529 per million British thermal units. January gas deliveries at the San Juan/Blanco Hub were last assessed at $3.19-$3.22, compared with Wednesday's $3.15-$3.23.

Firm, peak electricity for next-day delivery at Palo Verde (PV) in Arizona rose to $23.50-$25.00 a megawatt hour (MW), up from Wednesday's $22.00-$23.00. Power prices with similar delivery terms at the California-Oregon Border (COB) jumped to $23.00-$24.00, up from $21.50-$22.50 on Wednesday.
"It's basically been in oscillation for the past few days," said a New York broker.
January 1997 COB futures have been bouncing between $23.30 and $24.65 since Monday and January PV between $23.75 and $25.25.

Despite outlook for colder weather next week in the West, the market remained wary of heavy precipitation in the Pacific Northwest the past couple of weeks, and its effect on hydroelectric production for 1997, brokers and traders said.
"The water situation is high. It's in the back of people's mind. People are not going out the limb on that yet," the New York broker said.
January COB settled near its session high, up 55 cents at $24.45. February COB finished down five cents at $18.95. Deferred COB months were mostly inactive.
January PV settled at $24.68, up 24 cents after traded between $24.00 and $24.95. February PV finished down three cents at $19.43. Other active PV contracts ended mixed.
"It's pretty rangebound right now. What's going to break it out of the pattern is either weather or gas," said a Northwest futures trader.
NYMEX estimated 195 COB and 114 PV contracts were sold.
